question: Should explicitly configured, already-installed Codex `workspace-directory` plugins be admitted into OpenClaw’s native app ownership and approval pipeline?
rationale: Codex supplies the protocol, but organization-scoped catalog admission expands OpenClaw’s trusted plugin and application boundary; the protected label and prior marketplace revert make this an intentional maintainer product-security choice.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in
options.body: Support only exact configured workspace identities, request the catalog only when needed, preserve default-deny policy controls, and keep installation and authentication outside OpenClaw.

options.title: Retain curated-only
options.body: Keep organization workspace plugins outside the native policy pipeline and document the curated-only boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in
recommendation.body: Support only exact configured workspace identities, request the catalog only when needed, preserve default-deny policy controls, and keep installation and authentication outside OpenClaw.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged revert establishing the current boundary and directly inspected the relevant Codex contract.
